title: Part Three, Chapter 9: The First Dawn

verses.t: And this was the dawning and appearing of the sun, the moon and the stars.

And Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam rejoiced greatly when they saw the morning star, which came out first, shining, and came out first before the sun. And then they unwrapped the copal or incense they had brought from there in the East: "It will serve afterwards," they had said in their hearts; and then they unwrapped the three gifts they had thought of in their hearts. And the incense that Balam-quitzé brought was called Mixtampon, and the second, which Balam-acab brought, was called Caviztampon, and the one that Mahucutah brought was called Cahavilpon; and those three had only incense. And this they burned as they went dancing towards the East, and they wept for sweetness; and as they danced they burned their copal, the beloved and precious incense, and they wept because they did not see the sun, nor had it appeared. And then, when the sun came out, all the animals, small and great, rejoiced, and all came out from the paths of the water and from the ravines and stood on the peaks of the mountains, and all turned their faces towards the rising sun. And then they all sang and cried out, the puma and the jaguar; and the first to sing was the bird called Queletza; and truly all the animals rejoiced; and the eagle and the white vulture spread their wings, and all the birds, small and great. And the lords and their vassals were on their knees, those of Tanub and Ylocab, with those of Rabinal and the Cakchiquels, those of Quiquinaha and Tulhalha, Vchabaha, Quibaha, Ahbatena, and those of Yaqui-tepeu, and as many peoples as there were and are now, whose names cannot be counted; and the dawn came for all of them together. And then the earth was dried by the sun; and the sun was like a man when it appeared and burned, and it dried the whole face of the earth; and before the sun rose, everything was wet and muddy. And the sun rose up like a man, and its heat was not strong, but it only showed itself when it was born; and only its mirror remained, for this is surely not the sun that shines now, say the traditions. And then the gods Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz turned to stone, and also the gods of the puma, the jaguar, the viper, the cantí snake and the goblin; and they only clung to the trees when the sun, the moon and the stars came out; everywhere they all turned into stone. Perhaps we would not be standing now, because of the ravenous and biting animals, the puma, the jaguar, the viper, the cantí snake and the goblins! And perhaps the first animals were not turned to stone by the sun! And when it came out, Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam rejoiced greatly in their hearts; they rejoiced when it dawned. And the men were not many then, but were few, when they were on the mountains of Hacavitz, where the dawn came for them. And there they burned the copal and danced towards the East, from where they had come; and there is their homeland; from there came Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam, for these were their names. And there they grew and multiplied upon the mountain, and this was their town; and there they were when the sun, the moon and the stars came out, and it dawned and the whole face of the earth and of the world grew bright. And there began their song called Camucú, which they sang in the weeping of their hearts; they said in their song: "Alas, we were lost at Tulanzú; we were scattered! And our kinsmen and brothers stayed behind there! Why, we have seen the sun; why, the dawn has come for us!" they said to their companions, those of Yaqui. And likewise Tohil is the god of those of Yaqui, who are called Yolcuat and Quitzalcuat. "And we divided there at Tulanzú, and this was our coming out together to this place, and this is our being complete," they said among themselves, when they remembered their kinsmen back there, those of Yaqui, for whom the dawn came there in Mexico, as it is now called. And part of the people also stayed there in the East, who are called Tepeu-Oliman; and they stayed there, they said. And great was the pain and sorrow of their hearts there upon Hacavitz; and those of Tanub and Ylocab did the same; and likewise another people called Dan are there in the forest. And there the dawn came for the vassals of Tanub with their god, who likewise was Tohil, for the name of the god of the three tribes or clans of the Quiché was one; and so is the name of the god of the people of Rabinal, except that the name differs a little, for he is called Toh; and so our language is almost the same as that of Rabinal. And likewise the language of the Cakchiquels is different, because the name of their god was different when they came from Tulanzú; Tzotziha-Chimalcan is the name of their god, and so their language is different now. Like their god, they took their name from their homeland and their branch, and they are called Ahpozotzil-Ahpoxa. And likewise their language was changed with the god: when their god was given them there at Tulanzú, behind the stone, their language was changed, when they came from Tulanzú in the darkness. And together they were settled, and the dawn came for all the peoples, and the names of the gods were in order, in each of the tribes. And now we shall tell of the stay and the waiting on the mountain where all four were together: Balam-quitzé, Balam-acab, Mahucutah and Yquibalam; and their hearts wept over Tohil, Avilix and Hacavitz, who had been left by them among the bromeliads or grasses and in the moss.
